r1159104291: An archipelago of over 14,000 islands running along the Pacific coast of East Asia, stretching from the Sea of Okhotsk to the East China and Philippine seas.
Made up of three island arcs: the Northeastern Japan Arc, the Southwestern Japan Arc, and the Ryukyu Island Arc.
The largest island country in East Asia and the fourth-largest island country in the world.
r1159104631: Comprises two main landmasses, the North Island and the South Island, plus over 700 smaller islands, east of Australia across the Tasman Sea.
Its rugged terrain, including the Southern Alps, was shaped by tectonic uplift and volcanic activity.
Among the last large habitable landmasses settled by humans; Polynesians arrived between about 1280 and 1350 and developed Māori culture.
The Dutch explorer Abel Tasman sighted it in 1642, and Captain James Cook mapped it for Britain in 1769.
r1159104607: Bordered by the Arctic Ocean to the north, the Atlantic to the east, and the Pacific to the south and west.
The third-largest continent by area, after Asia and Africa.
Split into the subregions of Northern America (Canada, the US, Greenland) and Middle America (Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean).
m1159115321: An intercontinental sea almost entirely enclosed by land between Europe, Asia and Africa, linked to the Atlantic only through the narrow Strait of Gibraltar.
Also connects to the Black Sea via the Bosporus and to the Red Sea via the Suez Canal.
Includes marginal seas such as the Aegean, Adriatic, Tyrrhenian and Marmara.
Around 5.9 million years ago it was cut off from the Atlantic and largely dried up during the Messinian salinity crisis, before being refilled by the Zanclean flood.
r1159102893: A volcanic archipelago in Melanesia, east of northern Australia and northeast of New Caledonia.
First inhabited by Melanesian peoples; a Spanish expedition led by Fernandes de Queirós reached it in 1606.
Jointly administered by Britain and France as the New Hebrides from 1906 until independence as Vanuatu in 1980.
m1159115123: The third-largest of the world's oceanic divisions, bounded by Asia to the north, Africa to the west and Australia to the east.
Geologically the youngest ocean, having formed as the Tethys Ocean fragmented around 20 million years ago.
It is the warmest of the oceans and strongly influences global climate through its interaction with the atmosphere.
e1159105715: The highest mountain on Earth above sea level, lying in the Himalayas on the China-Nepal border at its summit.
Known as Sagarmatha in Nepali and Chomolangma in Tibetan.
Climbed via two main routes, from the southeast in Nepal or from the north in China; hundreds of climbers have died on its slopes.
Many bodies remain on the mountain because retrieving them is too dangerous.
vQ3783: Carries the largest discharge volume of any river in the world and rivals the Nile for the title of longest.
Its most distant source is in the Peruvian Andes, feeding the Ucayali and Marañón rivers that join to form its main stem.
Manaus, the largest city on the river, sits at the confluence of the Rio Negro and the Solimões, known as the Meeting of Waters.
m1159115461: The world's largest inland body of water, an endorheic basin situated between the Caucasus, Central Asia and the Iranian Plateau.
Bordered by Kazakhstan, Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran and Turkmenistan, and fed mainly by the Volga, Europe's longest river.
Its name comes from the ancient Caspi people who once lived along its shores.
m1159115037: The southernmost waters of the World Ocean, encircling Antarctica south of 60°S latitude.
Its deepest point, surveyed in 2019 by the Five Deeps Expedition at over 7,400 m, has been proposed for the name Factorian Deep.
James Cook's voyages in the 1770s first proved that open water encircled the southern polar latitudes.
m1159115879: Lies between Great Britain, Scandinavia and continental Europe, connecting to the Atlantic via the English Channel and the Norwegian Sea.
A major fishery and shipping route, and a significant source of offshore wind and oil and gas.
Was the centre of the Vikings' rise and later a focus of Hanseatic, Dutch and British competition for trade and sea power.
r1159104309: The longest continental mountain range in the world, running along the entire western edge of South America through seven countries.
Its highest peak, Aconcagua in Argentina, is the tallest mountain outside Asia.
Hosts high plateaus, including the Altiplano, the world's second-highest after Tibet, on which major cities like La Paz and Bogotá sit.
r1730071301: A French territory in the southwest Pacific, southwest of Vanuatu and east of Australia.
Its main island, Grande Terre, is nicknamed 'le Caillou' by locals; pro-independence Kanak parties call the territory Kanaky.
The indigenous Melanesian Kanak people make up 41% of the population.
m1159115379: A sea of the North Atlantic bounded by the Greater and Lesser Antilles, South America, and Central America.
Its deepest point, the Cayman Trough, reaches nearly 7,700 m below sea level.
Home to the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, the world's second-largest barrier reef system.
vQ5089: Rises in the western Himalayas and flows through North India before entering Bangladesh, where it is known as the Padma.
Joins the Brahmaputra and Meghna to form a vast delta emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
Considered sacred in Hinduism and central to the religious and cultural life of northern India.
r1159104133: The largest island in Europe and the ninth-largest in the world, comprising England, Scotland and Wales.
Was connected to mainland Europe by a land bridge, Doggerland, until it was submerged around 9,000 years ago.
Has been inhabited by modern humans for roughly 30,000 years.
vQ3503: Africa's deepest river, with measured depths around 220 m, and the second-longest on the continent after the Nile.
The only major river to cross the equator twice, as it loops through the Congo Basin.
Known historically as the Zaire River; its basin covers about 13% of Africa's total land area.
r1159104343: A peninsula in southwestern Europe occupied mainly by Spain and Portugal, separated from the rest of the continent by the Pyrenees.
Also includes Andorra, Gibraltar and a small part of southern France.
The second-largest peninsula in Europe by area, after the Scandinavian Peninsula.
r1159104311: The largest mountain system in North America, stretching from western Canada to New Mexico.
Formed 55 to 80 million years ago during the Laramide orogeny, when oceanic plates slid beneath the continent.
Distinct from the younger Cascade Range and Sierra Nevada further west.
r1159104127: The largest Indonesian island entirely within the country's territory and the sixth-largest island in the world.
Separated from the Malay Peninsula by the narrow Strait of Malacca and from Java by the Sunda Strait.
The volcanic Bukit Barisan mountains run the length of the island as its backbone.
m1159116607: The northernmost arm of the Mediterranean Sea, separating the Italian Peninsula from the Balkans.
Contains more than 1,300 islands, mostly along its eastern coast.
Its waters are less saline than the rest of the Mediterranean because it collects about a third of the sea's fresh water inflow.
vQ7355: China's second-longest river, named for the yellow colour its water takes on from sediment picked up on the Loess Plateau.
Rises in the Bayan Har Mountains and loops through the Ordos Plateau before reaching the North China Plain.
Its basin is considered the cradle of ancient Chinese civilization, traditionally linked to the founding of the Xia dynasty.
r1159104355: A subregion of Oceania made up of roughly 2,000 small islands in the northwestern Pacific.
Includes the Caroline, Gilbert, Mariana and Marshall Islands archipelagos.
Politically divided among six sovereign nations and territories, including Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia and Kiribati.
r1159104121: The world's second-largest island, separated from Australia by the narrow Torres Strait.
Shares the continental shelf with Australia; the two were joined as the landmass of Sahul during past ice ages.
Has the third-largest remaining rainforest in the world and the highest plant biodiversity of any island.
Politically split between Papua New Guinea in the east and Indonesia's Papua provinces in the west.
r1159104259: A peninsula in West Asia, also known as Asia Minor, that makes up most of Turkey's land area.
Bounded by the Mediterranean, Aegean and Black seas, with the Sea of Marmara separating it from Thrace in Europe.
An early centre of farming in the Neolithic period, from which agriculture spread into Europe roughly 9,000 years ago.
p1159104725: An external territory of Australia in the Pacific, between New Zealand and New Caledonia.
Served as a British penal settlement from 1788 to 1855, then was resettled in 1856 by descendants of the Bounty mutineers from Pitcairn Island.
Its native Norfolk Island pine is a symbol of the island.
r1159103795: The third-largest and most southerly of Japan's four main islands.
Historically known as Tsukushi-no-shima and governed through the Dazaifu administrative centre established under the 8th-century Taihō Code.
Some traditions hold it was once home to an independent dynasty with a culture distinct from Honshu's.
xQ524: A stratovolcano on the Gulf of Naples, part of the Campanian volcanic arc, a short distance from Naples.
Its 79 AD eruption buried the Roman cities of Pompeii, Herculaneum and Stabiae under ash and pumice.
The only volcano on Europe's mainland to have erupted within the last hundred years, with about three million people living nearby.
r1159102909: A volcanic archipelago in the Pacific straddling the equator, about 900 km west of mainland South America.
Famous for its endemic species, studied by Charles Darwin in the 1830s, which helped inspire his theory of evolution by natural selection.
Discovered by Europeans only in 1535, by Bishop Tomás de Berlanga, after limited pre-Columbian contact.
r1159102853: The largest and most populous island of Spain's Canary Islands, off the northwest coast of Africa.
Dominated by Teide, a volcanic peak that is the highest mountain in Spain and in the Atlantic islands.
Was home to the Indigenous Guanche people before its conquest by the Crown of Castile in 1496.
m1159115253: The northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, lying between the Indian subcontinent and the Indochinese Peninsula.
Receives major rivers including the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Irrawaddy.
Its coast includes the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest.
r1159103937: An arc of mountains across Central and Southeast Europe, the third-longest range in Europe after the Urals and Scandinavian Mountains.
Its highest peaks rise in the Tatra Mountains, closely followed by Romania's Southern Carpathians.
Provide habitat for Europe's largest populations of brown bears, wolves, chamois and lynxes.
r1159103785: An Indonesian island east of Borneo and the world's 11th-largest island.
Shaped by four peninsulas separated by the Gulf of Tomini, Gulf of Tolo and Gulf of Boni.
Separated from Borneo to the west by the Makassar Strait.
r1159104601: An archipelago off northwestern Europe comprising Great Britain, Ireland, the Isle of Man and thousands of smaller islands.
Includes two sovereign states, the Republic of Ireland and the United Kingdom.
Contains some of the oldest rocks on Earth, dated to 2.7 billion years, found in Ireland, Wales and northwest Scotland.
r1159103831: The largest island of the Society Islands in French Polynesia, formed from two eroded, now-extinct shield volcanoes joined by an isthmus.
Hosts Papeʻete, the capital of French Polynesia, and the region's only international airport.
Settled by Polynesians between about 900 and 1100 CE.
vQ41179: A transboundary river rising on the Tibetan Plateau and flowing through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.
Known as the Lancang River within China.
A major trade route between Tibet and Southeast Asia, though seasonal flow extremes make navigation difficult.
Hydroelectric dam building since the 2000s has disrupted its ecosystem and worsened droughts downstream.
m1159115861: A shallow marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean, divided between Norwegian and Russian waters.
Bordered by the Kola Peninsula, Svalbard, Franz Josef Land and Novaya Zemlya.
Warming faster than much of the Arctic, a process sometimes called 'Atlantification'.
m1159117319: A marginal sea of the North Pacific, forming the divide between Eurasia and the Americas along with the Bering Strait.
Named after Vitus Bering, the Danish-born Russian navigator who first explored it systematically in 1728.
Bordered by Alaska, the Russian Far East, the Kamchatka Peninsula and the Aleutian Islands.
m1159118439: An arm of the Mediterranean Sea off the northwest coast of Italy.
Thought to be named after the ancient Ligures people who once inhabited the region.
m1159115935: Separates the islands of Ireland, the Isle of Man and Great Britain.
Connects to the Celtic Sea via St George's Channel and to Scotland's inner seas via the North Channel.
Carries major passenger and freight traffic between Great Britain and Ireland.
r1159104327: A physiographic region of Asia covering most of the Himalayas and the land south of them, projecting into the Indian Ocean between the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea.
Politically split among Bangladesh, India and Pakistan, whose territories were part of British India before its 1947 partition.
Distinguished from the broader term 'South Asia', which also includes Nepal, Bhutan, the Maldives and Sri Lanka.
vQ973: A major Siberian river that, with its tributary the Irtysh, forms the world's seventh-longest river system.
Forms at the confluence of the Biya and Katun rivers, which originate in the Altai Mountains, and flows north into the Arctic Ocean.
Novosibirsk, Siberia's largest city, sits on its banks where the Trans-Siberian Railway crosses the river.
Its outlet, the Gulf of Ob, is the world's longest estuary.
r1159104143: An archipelago in eastern Indonesia, historically known as the Spice Islands for the nutmeg, mace and cloves found only there.
That spice trade drew European colonial interest from the 16th century onward.
Split in 1999 into Maluku Province, with a larger Christian population centred on Ambon, and North Maluku, predominantly Muslim with its capital at Sofifi.
m1159115987: A marginal sea of the northeastern Indian Ocean, bounded by Myanmar and Thailand and separated from the Bay of Bengal by the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Historically known as the Burma Sea; its coral reefs and islands are popular tourist destinations.
Its fishing and tourism infrastructure was severely damaged by the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami.
m1159115999: A marginal sea of the western Pacific between mainland China and the Korean Peninsula, also known as the North Sea.
Forms the northwestern extension of the East China Sea.
vQ1469: The longest river in France, rising in the Massif Central and flowing north then west to the Atlantic at Saint-Nazaire.
Its lower and central valley, dotted with vineyards and châteaux, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Gives its name to six French departments, including Loire and Loire-Atlantique.
e1159105881: A peak in the Greater Caucasus on the border between Azerbaijan and Russia's Dagestan region.
The highest point in both Azerbaijan and Dagestan.
Its name means 'turn to the market, bazaar', recalling medieval multinational fairs once held nearby in the Shahnabad Valley.
vQ552: Central Europe's Oder rises in the Czech Republic and flows through western Poland.
Forms part of the Oder-Neisse line, the border between Poland and Germany, for 187 km.
Empties into the Szczecin Lagoon and then the Baltic Sea's Bay of Pomerania.
m1159116517: The easternmost arm of the Baltic Sea, lying between Finland and Estonia, with Saint Petersburg at its eastern end.
The river Neva drains into it at Saint Petersburg, making it a strategically important seaway for Russia.
Helsinki and Tallinn, on opposite shores, have been proposed to be linked by an undersea tunnel beneath the gulf.
r1159104155: A peninsula in the Russian Far East, bounded by the Sea of Okhotsk to the west and the Bering Sea to the east.
Home to the volcanoes of Kamchatka, part of the Pacific Ring of Fire and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Most of its roughly 320,000 inhabitants live in Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky and nearby Yelizovo.
m1159115441: A large inland sea of saltwater in northeastern Canada, politically part of Nunavut though bordered by Ontario, Quebec and Manitoba.
Connects to the Atlantic via the Hudson Strait and to the Arctic Ocean via the Foxe Channel.
Its drainage basin extends south into several U.S. states, including Minnesota and Montana.
Its southern arm is known as James Bay.
r1159102793: Sweden's largest island, home to the main town of Visby and smaller islands including Fårö and Gotska Sandön.
Historically spoke the distinct Gutnish language before Swedish became dominant.
Fully integrated into Sweden with no special autonomy, unlike some other European offshore island groups.
r1159103861: An Indonesian and Timorese archipelago, now officially called the Nusa Tenggara Islands, meaning 'Southeast Islands'.
Mostly lies within the Wallacea biogeographic region, except Bali, which sits on the Sunda Shelf.
Part of the volcanic Sunda Arc formed by subduction along the Sunda Trench.
r1159102765: The westernmost of the Lesser Sunda Islands, east of Java and west of Lombok.
Indonesia's only Hindu-majority province, with over 86% of residents practising Balinese Hinduism.
Its arts, dance, sculpture and music have made it Indonesia's leading tourist destination, with tourism making up 80% of its economy.
r1159103873: An arc of Caribbean islands running from near Puerto Rico southeast through the Leeward and Windward Islands before turning west along Venezuela's coast.
Distinguished from the larger Greater Antilles to the west; together they form the Antilles within the West Indies.
Partly volcanic in origin, and historically dominated by the Indigenous Kalinago people, unlike the more diverse Greater Antilles.
vQ14294: The longest river on the Iberian Peninsula, rising in mid-eastern Spain and flowing west to the Atlantic.
Empties into the ocean at Lisbon, Portugal's capital, which grew up around its estuary.
r1730071111: A peninsula in southern Greece, the southernmost region of the Balkans, linked to the mainland by the Isthmus of Corinth.
Known from the late Middle Ages until the 19th century as the Morea.
The isthmus separates the Gulf of Corinth from the Saronic Gulf.
p1159105067: An isolated volcanic island in the South Atlantic, roughly midway between Africa and South America.
Part of the British Overseas Territory of Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha.
Discovered by Portuguese navigator João da Nova in 1501 and named for Ascension Day in 1503.
Served as an important refuelling stop for ships and flying boats, and as an Allied air and naval base in World War II.
vQ1265: Rises in the Rocky Mountains of Colorado and flows southwest across the Colorado Plateau, carving the Grand Canyon.
Its name, Spanish for 'colored reddish', reflects its historically heavy silt load.
Almost its entire flow is diverted by dams and aqueducts, supplying water to about 40 million people across the US Southwest and Mexico.
r1159104625: The larger of New Zealand's two main islands by area, though less populous than the North Island.
Shaped by the Southern Alps, which include Aoraki/Mount Cook, New Zealand's highest peak.
Its east side holds the Canterbury Plains, while the west coast and Fiordland are known for rugged coastlines and native bush.
r1159104191: A mountain range in eastern North America running about 3,300 km from central Alabama to Newfoundland.
Geologically related to the Scottish Highlands, Atlas Mountains and Scandinavian Mountains, all once part of the ancient Central Pangean Mountains.
Formed over hundreds of millions of years, beginning with the creation of the supercontinent Rodinia around 1.1 billion years ago.
m1159115219: A marginal sea of the South Pacific off northeastern Australia, named for its numerous islands and reefs.
Contains the Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest reef system and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1981.
Site of the Battle of the Coral Sea, a major World War II naval confrontation between Japan and the Allies.
r1159104181: A Central and South Asian mountain range at the junction of the Tian Shan, Karakoram, Kunlun, Hindu Kush and Himalayas.
Mostly located in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region, with the Wakhan Corridor bordering it to the south.
Known since the Victorian era as the 'Roof of the World'.
m1159119199: A gulf at the northern tip of the Red Sea, southeast of the Sinai Peninsula.
Its coastline is shared by Egypt, Israel, Jordan and Saudi Arabia.
vQ128102: The chief tributary of the Ob and the longest tributary river in the world.
Rises in the Mongolian Altai near the border between China and Mongolia.
Together with the Ob, drains most of Western Siberia and the Altai Mountains.
r1159103345: A historical and cultural region in northwestern France, roughly matching the former Duchy of Normandy.
Includes both mainland France and the British Channel Islands of Guernsey and Jersey.
Takes its name from Viking ('Northmen') settlers who arrived from the 9th century, formalized by a 10th-century treaty with the Viking jarl Rollo.
Launching point of the 1066 Norman conquest of England, which tied Normandy and England together for nearly 150 years.
m1159115233: A marginal sea of the South Pacific separating Australia and New Zealand.
Named after Dutch explorer Abel Tasman, the first known European to cross it, in 1642.
Later extensively navigated by James Cook during his 1770s voyages of exploration.
e1159106673: A large sandstone monolith near the centre of Australia's Northern Territory, also known as Ayers Rock.
Sacred to the Pitjantjatjara Aboriginal people, with surrounding springs, waterholes and ancient rock paintings.
A UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Australia's most recognisable natural landmarks.
m1159116081: Lies southeast of the Malay Archipelago, overlying the continental shelf between Australia and Western New Guinea.
Part of the western Pacific Ocean separating Indonesia from Australia.
p1159105051: The world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, dropping over the edge of the Auyán-tepui mountain in Venezuela.
Located within Canaima National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Gran Sabana region.
Feeds into the Churún and Carrao rivers, tributaries of the Orinoco.
e1159105929: A near-symmetric pyramidal peak of the Pennine Alps straddling the border between Switzerland and Italy.
Often called the 'Mountain of Mountains' and considered among the most photographed mountains in the world.
Overlooks the Swiss resort town of Zermatt to the northeast and Italy's Breuil-Cervinia to the south.
r1159102855: The third-largest and second-most-populous of Spain's Canary Islands, off northwest Africa.
Its capital, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, is the largest city in the Canary Islands and the ninth-largest in Spain.
Rises to 1,956 m at Morro de la Agujereada, making it the third-highest island in the archipelago.
vQ160636: Rises in south-central Colorado and flows to the Gulf of Mexico, forming much of the US-Mexico border.
Known as the Río Bravo in Mexico.
Its fertile valley is a vital water source for seven US and Mexican states across arid and semi-arid land.
r1159102817: One of Spain's Balearic Islands, its name meaning 'smaller island' in contrast to nearby Mallorca.
Its capital, Mahón, and the town of Ciutadella de Menorca are its main ports.
Its highest point, El Toro, rises only 358 m above sea level.
vQ173017: Rises in South Africa and flows east through Mozambique to the Indian Ocean, the second-largest African river draining to that ocean after the Zambezi.
First sighted by a European when Vasco da Gama anchored off its mouth in 1498, naming it the River of the Holy Spirit.
Geologically, its upper course once carried the Zambezi's flow until tectonic uplift redirected the drainage divide.
p1159105055: An uninhabited coral atoll in the eastern Pacific, the only French territory in the North Pacific.
Claimed by both France and Mexico; Mexico established a small military colony there in 1905.
During the Mexican Revolution the colony was largely abandoned after most colonists died and a lighthouse keeper briefly ruled the island as self-declared king.
vQ4915: Flows from Pittsburgh to its mouth on the Mississippi, forming the boundary between the Midwestern and Southern United States.
The largest tributary by volume of the Mississippi River and the sixth-oldest river on the North American continent.
Served as a key transportation route for pioneers during westward expansion in the 18th and 19th centuries.
r1159102859: A densely populated island in southeastern New York, extending into the Atlantic and comprising Brooklyn, Queens, Nassau and Suffolk counties.
Shaped largely by glacial processes during the Pleistocene, including terminal moraines and outwash plains.
Brooklyn and Queens, its western boroughs, are part of New York City, while Nassau and Suffolk form its more suburban east.
r1159104599: The world's largest archipelago by area, lying between mainland Southeast Asia and Australia with over 25,000 islands.
Spans Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei, East Timor and Papua New Guinea.
Also known historically as the East Indies or Nusantara.
vQ134350: A major river of Central and Eastern Europe, once called 'the most Hungarian river' for flowing entirely within the medieval Kingdom of Hungary.
Rises in Ukraine's Chornohora mountains and flows through Romania, Slovakia, Hungary and Serbia before joining the Danube.
Contributes about 13% of the Danube's total runoff.
e1159107911: A dormant shield volcano on the island of Hawaii, the highest point in Hawaii, about 38 m taller than its massive neighbour Mauna Loa.
Measured from its base on the ocean floor, it rises more than Everest's height above sea level, leading some to call it the tallest mountain in the world.
About one million years old, it has passed its most active shield-building stage and now erupts thicker, more viscous lava.
r1159104005: A narrow Mexican peninsula separating the Gulf of California from the Pacific Ocean.
Stretches from Mexicali in the north to Cabo San Lucas in the south, with about 65 offshore islands.
Separated from mainland Mexico by the Gulf of California and the Colorado River, and home to four distinct desert regions.
e1159106753: The highest mountain on mainland Australia, located on the Main Range of the Snowy Mountains in New South Wales.
Named after the Polish national hero Tadeusz Kościuszko.
Lies within Kościuszko National Park, part of the Australian Alps National Parks and Reserves.
m1159120667: A region of the Atlantic Ocean bounded by four currents forming the North Atlantic Gyre, and the only named sea without land boundaries.
Known for its distinctive brown Sargassum seaweed and unusually calm, clear blue water.
Bermuda lies near its western fringe.
l1159126669: A saline lake in Kenya's Rift Valley, the world's largest permanent desert lake and largest alkaline lake.
Ranks fourth in the world by volume among salt lakes, after the Caspian Sea, Issyk-Kul and Lake Van.
Threatened by Ethiopia's Gilgel Gibe III Dam, which has reduced the flow of the Omo River that supplies most of its water.
m1159117723: A strait connecting the North Sea and the Kattegat, running between Denmark, Norway and Sweden.
One of the busiest shipping routes in the world and historically the only access to the Baltic Sea before the Eider Canal was built in 1784.
Held strategic importance for Germany in both World Wars.
e1159108689: A stratovolcano in Ecuador's Cordillera Occidental, part of the Andes, last known to have erupted around AD 550.
Ecuador's highest mountain, though well below Everest's elevation above sea level.
Due to Earth's equatorial bulge, its summit is the point on the planet's surface farthest from the Earth's center.
r1159102787: Estonia's largest and most populous island, the main island of the West Estonian archipelago in the Baltic Sea.
Known historically in much of the world as Ösel from the 13th century until the early 20th century.
Its administrative centre is the town of Kuressaare.
r1159104073: An arid region straddling northwestern India and Pakistan, one of the largest subtropical deserts in Asia.
About two-thirds of it lies in India, mostly in Rajasthan, bordered by the Aravalli Range to the east.
Formed partly because an ice sheet over the Tibetan Plateau during the last glacial maximum weakened the monsoon, leading to desertification.
vQ14383: The longest and largest-by-volume tributary of the Danube, rising in Slovenia and flowing through Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Joins the Danube at Belgrade, Serbia's capital.
Its basin is shared by three national capitals: Ljubljana, Zagreb and Belgrade.
r1159103101: A forested, hilly natural region spanning Belgium, Luxembourg, and parts of France and Germany.
Geologically a western extension of the Eifel, both uplifted during the Devonian period roughly 383 million years ago.
Covers most of southeastern Wallonia and forms the northern third of Luxembourg, where it is called the Oesling.
l1159126761: An endorheic salt lake in Iranian Azerbaijan, once the largest lake in West Asia and the sixth-largest saltwater lake on Earth.
Shrank to about 10% of its former size by 2017 due to drought, river damming and groundwater pumping.
Nearly dried up entirely by 2025 despite temporary recoveries from rainfall and water diversion efforts.
m1159120167: Bounded to the north by Sulawesi and to the south by the islands of Flores and Sumbawa in Indonesia.
Lies within the Coral Triangle, a global centre of marine biodiversity among Indonesia's seas.
r1159103951: A mountain range in the western United States, mostly in California, forming part of the American Cordillera's western backbone.
Home to Mount Whitney, the highest point in the contiguous US, and Lake Tahoe, the largest alpine lake in North America.
Yosemite Valley, carved by glaciers from hundred-million-year-old granite, lies within its boundaries.
Hosts the General Sherman Tree, the largest tree in the world by volume, within Sequoia National Park.
vQ8168: The sixth-longest river in Europe, flowing from northwest Russia into the Arctic Ocean.
Lies mostly in the Komi Republic, with its northernmost reaches crossing the Nenets Autonomous Okrug.
vQ14369: A right tributary of the Danube flowing through Switzerland, Austria and Germany, the third-largest Danube tributary by discharge.
Its drainage basin's highest point is the summit of Piz Bernina.
The Engadine valley it flows through is the only Swiss valley whose waters eventually reach the Black Sea.
r1159104187: One of the longest mountain chains in Asia, running over 3,000 km along the northern edge of the Tibetan Plateau in western China.
Known in China as the 'Forefather of Mountains'.
According to the historian Sima Qian, Emperor Wu of Han named the range after sending men to find the Yellow River's source.
e1159106291: A desert valley in eastern California's northern Mojave Desert, recorded as the hottest surface location on Earth.
Furnace Creek within the valley holds the highest reliably recorded air temperature on the planet, 54.4°C in 2020 and 2021.
Forms the principal feature of the Mojave and Colorado Deserts Biosphere Reserve.
vQ191829: Colombia's main river, flowing north through the western half of the country and giving its name to the Magdalena River Valley.
Named after the biblical Mary Magdalene.
Navigable through much of its lower reaches up to the town of Honda, despite shifting sandbars at its delta.
r1159103773: A large Arctic Archipelago island straddling Nunavut and the Northwest Territories, Canada's second-largest island.
The eighth-largest island in the world, slightly larger than Great Britain but smaller than Honshu.
Named after Queen Victoria; its small population is split between Cambridge Bay and Ulukhaktok.
e1159106815: The highest mountain in Scotland, the United Kingdom and the British Isles, at the western end of the Grampian Mountains near Fort William.
Its 700-metre cliffs on the north face offer some of Scotland's premier rock and ice climbing.
Has hosted a foot race to its summit since 1898 and was home to a staffed weather observatory from 1883 to 1904.
vQ166966: Formed at the confluence of the Euphrates and Tigris rivers near al-Qurnah in southern Iraq, flowing to the Persian Gulf.
Its southern stretch forms the border between Iraq and Iran.
Once held the world's largest date palm forest, with an estimated one-fifth of all the world's palm trees, before major losses from war and salinity.
r1730070381: An unincorporated US territory and atoll in the Pacific, closed to public entry and under US Air Force jurisdiction.
Used since 1934 as a naval refuelling depot, airbase, and testing site for nuclear, biological and chemical weapons, including Agent Orange storage.
Its surrounding waters are now protected as a National Wildlife Refuge within the Pacific Islands Heritage Marine National Monument.
l1159113265: Ethiopia's largest lake and the source of the Blue Nile, in the northwestern Ethiopian Highlands.
Fed by the Gilgel Abay, Reb and Gumara rivers, and regulated by a weir controlling flow to the Blue Nile Falls and a hydropower station.
m1159115717: One of four seas surrounding Indonesia's Maluku Islands, connected to the Pacific Ocean and encircled by hundreds of islands including Timor.
Stretches about 1,000 km east to west and 500 km north to south.
l1159115109: Armenia's largest lake and one of the largest freshwater alpine lakes in Eurasia, at nearly 1,900 m elevation.
Fed by 28 rivers and streams, with most of its water lost to evaporation rather than drainage.
Heavily exploited for irrigation and hydropower during the Soviet era, which sharply lowered its water level and turned Sevan Island into a peninsula.
m1159119235: Carries cold Arctic water south into the North Atlantic over the Denmark Strait cataract, the world's largest underwater waterfall.
r1159104221: Fertile low grasslands covering more than 1,200,000 km2 across Argentina, Uruguay and southern Brazil.
Interrupted only by the low Ventana and Tandil hills near Bahía Blanca and Tandil in Argentina.
Transformed by humans through the introduction of cattle, pigs and sheep grazing on the plains.
e1159105955: The highest mountain in Germany, in the Wetterstein Mountains, with the Austria-Germany border running across its western summit.
Home to Germany's largest glaciers, the Northern Schneeferner and Höllentalferner.
First climbed in 1820 by Josef Naus and companions; today reached via three main routes including the Jubilee Ridge.
l1159113595: One of the smaller African Great Lakes, located in the Albertine Rift on the border between the DR Congo and Uganda, just south of the equator.
Connects to Lake George to its north and drains south into Lake Albert via the Semliki River.
vQ93360: Chile's second-longest river, rising in Andean lakes and flowing to the Gulf of Arauco on the Pacific.
The widest river in Chile, with an average width of about 1 km.
Four bridges cross it in the Concepción metropolitan area.
r1159103935: A mountain range running the length of the Scandinavian Peninsula, forming Norway's dramatic fjords on its steep western slopes.
Forms much of the border between Norway and Sweden, reaching 2,000 m near the Arctic Circle.
Galdhøpiggen, its highest peak, is the tallest point in mainland Northern Europe.
vQ8319: A major Mississippi tributary rising from snowpack in Colorado's Sawatch and Mosquito mountain ranges.
The sixth-longest river in the United States, flowing east through Kansas, Oklahoma and Arkansas.
An 1859 gold discovery near its headwaters at Leadville, Colorado, drew a short-lived rush of prospectors.
m1159116731: Lies in the western Pacific between the Indonesian islands of Sulawesi, Halmahera and the Sula Islands.
Overlies the Molucca Sea Plate, a microplate being subducted in two opposite directions, making the sea prone to earthquakes.
e1159107205: An active stratovolcano on Sumbawa in Indonesia's Lesser Sunda Islands.
Its 1815 eruption was the largest in recorded history, ejecting up to 150 cubic kilometres of material at VEI-7.
The resulting global cooling caused 1816 to become known as the 'Year Without a Summer'.
m1159119215: A lake in northwestern Venezuela that, hydrologically, functions more like an estuary connected to the Gulf of Venezuela.
If counted as a lake, it would be South America's largest, and is among the oldest lakes on Earth at roughly 36 million years.
Rich in oil and gas; the surrounding area experiences the Catatumbo lightning, among the most frequent lightning activity on Earth.
r1159103863: A disputed archipelago in the South China Sea off the Philippines, Malaysia and Vietnam, named after a 19th-century British whaling captain.
Contains less than 200 hectares of natural land spread across hundreds of square kilometres of sea.
Its strategic shipping lanes and potential oil and gas reserves make its roughly 45 islands a flashpoint for competing territorial claims.
vQ204806: The major tributary of the Niger River and the second-longest river in Nigeria, also flowing through Cameroon.
Navigable for most of its length during summer months, making it an important regional transportation route.
Its name comes from a Tiv word meaning 'river or lake of hippos'.
m1159118457: The westernmost part of the Mediterranean Sea, lying between Spain and Morocco/Algeria.
The Strait of Gibraltar, connecting the Mediterranean to the Atlantic, lies at its western end.
r1159104101: The world's largest tropical wetland and largest flooded grassland, mostly within Brazil's Mato Grosso do Sul state.
Extends into Bolivia and Paraguay, with roughly 80% of its floodplains submerged during the rainy season.
Supports a biologically diverse range of aquatic plants and a dense array of animal species.
l1159126421: The largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere, in northern Utah, a remnant of the prehistoric Lake Bonneville.
Its area fluctuates greatly with a shallow average depth of under 5 m; it fell to a record low in 2021 after years of drought and water diversion.
Fed by the Jordan, Weber and Bear rivers, which deposit about 1.1 million tons of minerals into the lake each year.
m1159116927: Separates Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu, three of Japan's four main islands, linking the Pacific Ocean to the Sea of Japan.
Was the main transport link between the Kansai and Kyushu regions before the San'yo Main Line was built.
Connected by the Honshu-Shikoku Bridge Project since the 1980s, including the Great Seto Bridge.
r1159102695: A large coastal island in Brazil's Pará state, the second-largest island in South America.
Was home from around 400 BC to 1600 AD to the advanced Marajoara culture, which may have numbered over 100,000 people.
Today known for its large water buffalo population and the pororoca tidal bore in its surrounding rivers.
r1159104295: A system of mountain ranges, plateaus and hills running parallel to Australia's east coast, the longest mountain chain entirely within a single country.
Stretches over 3,500 km from the Torres Strait through Queensland, New South Wales and Victoria.
Serves as the main watershed for eastern Australia's river systems and includes several World Heritage Areas such as the Greater Blue Mountains.
e1159107181: The highest mountain in Malaysia and in Maritime Southeast Asia, on the island of Borneo in Sabah.
Protected within Kinabalu Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for exceptional biodiversity, including Rafflesia plants and orangutans.
A 1997 satellite resurvey of its summit, Low's Peak, found it slightly lower than previously published.
r1159104085: A narrow strip of land linking North and South America between the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean, home to the Panama Canal.
Formed around 3 million years ago, separating the Atlantic and Pacific and helping create the Gulf Stream.
Fossil evidence from the isthmus helped inspire Alfred Wegener's theory of continental drift.
r1159104531: A group of coral atolls and reefs in the central Indian Ocean, including the Great Chagos Bank, the world's largest atoll by area.
Over half its small total land area lies on Diego Garcia.
Holds a quarter to half of the Indian Ocean's reef area still in excellent condition, largely free of local pollution and development.
e1159105397: The southernmost active volcano on Earth, on Ross Island in Antarctica's Ross Dependency.
Named by Captain James Clark Ross in 1841 after his ship, HMS Erebus.
Has had a persistent lava lake in its summit crater since at least the early 1970s.
m1159116169: A marginal sea along the west side of the Antarctic Peninsula, named after Russian navigator Fabian von Bellingshausen, who explored it in 1821.
Reaches a maximum depth of about 4.5 km and connects to the Amundsen Sea to the west.
r1159102875: The largest uninhabited island in the world, in Baffin Bay within Canada's Arctic Archipelago.
Its highest point is the Devon Ice Cap, part of the Arctic Cordillera.
Its surface, including the Haughton impact crater, closely resembles Mars and has drawn scientific interest for that reason.
m1159116787: A gulf at the northwestern South China Sea, off northern Vietnam and South China.
Known in Chinese sources as Beibu Wan, or 'Northern Gulf'.
r1730074507: The largest island of Antarctica, lying in the Bellingshausen Sea west of Palmer Land.
The George VI Ice Shelf fills the sound separating it from the mainland, physically connecting it to Palmer Land.
The second-largest uninhabited island in the world, after Devon Island.
vQ182343: Flows north from Lake Erie to Lake Ontario, forming part of the Canada-US border and home to Niagara Falls.
Over 12,000 years, the falls have eroded roughly 11 km upstream, carving the gorge below them.
Hydroelectric stations on both the Canadian and American sides generate a combined 4.4 gigawatts of power.
m1159120073: Lies north of Bali and south of Kangean Island, forming the southwestern part of the Flores Sea.
The Madura Strait opens into it from the west.
vQ75745: A major river of Mongolia and Russia's Buryatia, draining into Lake Baikal and forming the most distant headwaters of the Yenisey-Angara system.
Supplies almost half of Lake Baikal's riverine inflow and forms a wide delta of 680 km2 where it enters the lake.
Subject to periodic floods, with three classified as catastrophic between 1730 and 1900.
r1159103391: The largest island in Indonesia's Maluku Islands, formerly known as Jilolo or Gilolo.
Home to Sofifi, the capital of North Maluku province.
Its population is roughly evenly split between Muslims and Christians.
r1159104045: The most extensive high plateau on Earth outside Tibet, spanning Bolivia, Peru, Chile and Argentina at the widest part of the Andes.
Home to Lake Titicaca, South America's largest lake, on the Bolivia-Peru border.
Was the site of pre-Columbian cultures including the Tiwanaku and the Inca Empire before Spanish conquest in the 16th century.
e1159105963: Slovenia's highest mountain and the highest peak of the Julian Alps.
The pre-eminent national symbol, appearing on Slovenia's coat of arms and flag.
Was also the highest peak in Yugoslavia before Slovenia's 1991 independence.
m1159118425: The southern part of the Aegean Sea, lying north of Crete and bounded by the Cyclades and Dodecanese islands.
Reaches depths of nearly 3,300 m off the northeastern coast of Crete.
Major ferry routes to Piraeus, Heraklion and the Dodecanese cross this sea.
r1159103597: The second of the two main Caucasus ranges, running parallel to the Greater Caucasus through the Armenian Highlands.
Separated from the Pontic range by the Kolkhida Lowland in the west and the Kura-Aras Lowland in the east.
Its western portion extends into eastern Turkey and northwestern Iran.
l1159122891: Sweden's third-largest freshwater lake, after Vänern and Vättern, draining into the Baltic Sea near Stockholm.
Its easternmost bay, Riddarfjärden, lies in central Stockholm.
Crossed by several bridges, including at Kvicksund and between Strängnäs and Enköping.
r1159103405: The third-largest island in the Philippines, in the Eastern Visayas, divided since 1965 into three provinces.
First sighted by a European when Ferdinand Magellan's expedition passed by in 1521.
Later the scene of a major uprising against American forces during the Philippine-American War, followed by a brutal pacification campaign.
r1159104093: An endorheic basin in China's Xinjiang region, the largest basin in northwest China, bounded by the Tian Shan and Kunlun mountains.
Dominated by the Taklamakan Desert and known historically to the Uyghur as Altishahr, meaning 'six cities'.
Now a major site for solar and wind energy development, with transmission lines ringing the desert.
l1159113439: The largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia, part of the Mekong river system in central Cambodia.
Designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve for its exceptional biodiversity.
Its water level swings dramatically with the seasons, rising up to 10 m higher after the monsoon.
r1159102545: The largest and most populous island of Portugal's Azores archipelago, nicknamed 'The Green Island'.
Home to Ponta Delgada, the Azores' largest city.
r1159103243: A highland region of mountains and plateaus covering about 15% of mainland France.
Shaped by volcanism that subsided within the last 10,000 years, separated from the Alps by the Rhône river valley.
Remained a barrier to transport within France until the A75 motorway opened access to the region.
r1159103837: Fiji's largest island, home to the national capital and largest city, Suva.
Houses the large majority of Fiji's population.
l1159114553: A high-altitude freshwater lake near Mount Kailash in Tibet, at about 4,600 m elevation.
Sacred in Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and the Bon religion, drawing pilgrims who trek to it and circle nearby Mount Kailash.
Overflows into the adjacent salt lake Rakshastal; the sources of the Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra and Karnali rivers lie nearby.
r1159102867: An uninhabited member of Canada's Queen Elizabeth Islands in the Arctic Archipelago, Canada's eighth-largest island.
Home to some of the largest mountains in the western Canadian Arctic, reaching about 750 m.
Split between the Northwest Territories and Nunavut along the 110th meridian west.
l1159113545: The largest lake in Sápmi and the third-largest in Finland, north of the Arctic Circle in Lapland.
Contains over 3,000 islands, including Hautuumaasaari, an ancient Sámi burial site, and the sacred Ukonkivi.
Drains northward through the Paatsjoki into the Barents Sea.
m1159118231: A strait separating Russia's Sakhalin Island from Japan's Hokkaido, linking the Sea of Japan with the Sea of Okhotsk.
Named after French naval officer Jean-François de Galaup, comte de Lapérouse, who explored it in 1787.
Known in Japan as the Sōya Strait.
r1159103099: A range along the Czech-German border separating Bohemia from Saxony.
Heavily shaped by centuries of mining, which also helped drive the early transformation of metallurgy into a large-scale industry preceding the Industrial Revolution.
Its highest peaks are the Klínovec in the Czech Republic and the Fichtelberg in Germany.
r1159103839: A group of islands in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar, including Mauritius and France's Réunion.
Named after Portuguese navigator Pedro Mascarenhas, who first visited in 1512.
Share a geological origin on the Mauritia microcontinent, once wedged between India and Madagascar before they separated about 70 million years ago.
e1159105349: An active stratovolcano in Cameroon, the highest point in sub-Saharan western and central Africa.
Part of the Cameroon Volcanic Line, which also includes Lake Nyos, site of a deadly 1986 gas disaster.
Erupted most recently in 2012, with an earlier 1909 eruption forcing German colonial authorities to relocate temporarily to Douala.
m1159117301: A strait between Mexico and Cuba connecting the Yucatán Basin of the Caribbean Sea with the Gulf of Mexico.
Reaches nearly 2,800 m deep near the Cuban coast.
r1159102869: A large island at the entrance to Hudson Bay, part of Canada's Arctic Archipelago, Canada's seventh-largest island.
Its only settlement, Coral Harbour, is known as Salliq in Inuktitut.
The only area in Nunavut that does not observe daylight saving time.
p1159104883: A rocky headland in South Africa, the southernmost point of South Africa and the geographic southern tip of the African continent.
Marks the traditional dividing line between the Atlantic and Indian oceans.
Historically notorious among sailors as a hazard on the clipper route, once known in English as Cape L'Agulhas.
vQ209530: The largest tributary of the Orange River and the longest river lying wholly within South Africa.
Became the main water source for the Witwatersrand mining region after the 19th-century gold rush.
The Vaal Dam, near Deneysville, regulates its flow.
r1159103407: The sixth-largest and fourth-most populous island in the Philippines, in the western Visayas.
Divided into four provinces, none of which bear the island's name, unlike other Visayan islands.
Bisected by the Central Panay Mountain Range, its longest mountain chain.
e1159105967: A mountain on the Czech Republic-Poland border, the highest point in the Czech Republic and in the entire Sudetes range.
The most prominent point of the Silesian Ridge within the Giant Mountains.
vQ191832: The second-longest right tributary of the Lena River, in Russia's Sakha Republic.
Formed part of the historic river route to Okhotsk; in 1639 Ivan Moskvitin used it to reach the Sea of Okhotsk.
Its basin is known for gold deposits and Cambrian-era fossils.
r1159103005: A mountainous region in northern Morocco, bounded by the Mediterranean, the Atlantic, and the Ouergha and Moulouya rivers.
Homeland of the Riffian Berber peoples and the heart of the short-lived Republic of the Rif, which fought Spanish colonial forces in the 1920s Rif War.
Split linguistically between an Arabized western Jebala and a predominantly Berber-speaking eastern Rif.
r1159104149: The northernmost cluster of islands in Canada's Arctic Archipelago, split between Nunavut and the Northwest Territories.
Hold roughly 14% of the world's glacier and ice cap area outside Greenland and Antarctica.
Their southern islands are known as the Parry Islands.
l1159106863: Straddles the Saskatchewan-Alberta border in northern Canada, mostly within Saskatchewan.
Fed by the Athabasca River, with its outflow continuing north via the Slave and Mackenzie rivers to the Arctic Ocean.
m1159117185: Lies between the Kutch and Saurashtra peninsulas in India's Gujarat state, opening toward the Arabian Sea.
Its southern coast, rich in marine life, includes protected parks and sanctuaries amid islands, mud flats and coral reefs.
Major shipping harbours including Kandla line its northern shore.
r1159103069: A mountain range on the Turkmenistan-Iran border, running about 650 km southeast of the Caspian Sea.
Part of the larger Alpide belt, bordering the Alborz mountains to the southwest.
Its highest peak in Turkmenistan, Mount Rizeh, lies near the capital Ashgabat.
r1159103461: The largest and highest island in Samoa, though significantly less populated than the smaller Upolu.
The sixth-largest island in Polynesia, after New Zealand's main islands and Hawaii's Hawaii and Maui.
Known in formal Samoan oratory by its classical name, Salafai.
e1159105931: Sweden's highest mountain, in the Scandinavian range in Swedish Lapland north of the Arctic Circle.
Has two main peaks; the glaciated southern peak, once the taller, has shrunk enough that the icefree northern peak is now highest.
Lies near the Kungsleden hiking trail between Abisko and Hemavan.
r1159102783: An island off the western coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, giving its name to the surrounding Nias archipelago.
The archipelago also includes the Batu Islands to the southeast and the Hinako Islands to the west.
r1159103897: A mountain range in Russia's Far East, extending about 900 km northeast from Vladivostok along the Pacific coast.
Its highest summit is Tordoki Yani.
r1159102915: An archipelago in the central South Pacific comprising independent Samoa and most of American Samoa, forming part of Polynesia.
Home to roughly 250,000 people who share the Samoan language and the fa'a Samoa culture.
The oldest known evidence of human activity dates to around 1050 BC, from a Lapita site on Upolu island.
l1159115429: The largest lake in Southern Europe, straddling the border of Albania and Montenegro.
A karst lake named after the Albanian city of Shkodër on its southeastern shore.
Its Montenegrin section is a national park, while the Albanian part is a protected Ramsar wetland site.
m1159120401: Surrounded by the Philippine islands of Masbate, Panay, Leyte, Cebu and Negros.
A major fishing ground for sardines, mackerel and herring, with an annual closed season to protect stocks.
Connects to the Sibuyan Sea, Samar Sea, Guimaras Strait and Camotes Sea.
r1159103131: An outlying subrange of the Rocky Mountain system rising from the Great Plains in South Dakota and Wyoming.
Sacred to the Lakota, who call it Pahá Sápa, after taking the territory from the Cheyenne in 1776.
Formed by the upwarping of ancient rock, later shaped by stream erosion into its present rugged topography.
r1159104049: An extensive plateau region covering roughly half of Brazil's land area across its eastern, southern and central portions.
Shaped largely by ancient basaltic lava flows, now geologically quiet with no active seismicity or volcanism.
Home to the vast majority of Brazil's population, including its narrow adjacent coastal strip.
vQ335575: The largest river in California, rising in the Klamath Mountains and flowing south through the fertile Sacramento Valley.
Drains into the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta and San Francisco Bay.
Historically supported one of the southernmost large Chinook salmon runs in North America and one of California's densest Native American populations.
r1159103171: A peninsula in Azerbaijan extending into the Caspian Sea, home to the capital Baku.
Often likened to the beak of the eagle shape of Azerbaijan's territory.
Ends in the dune spit of Shah Dili, the easternmost point of mainland Azerbaijan, now a national park.
r1159102951: A subantarctic archipelago of New Zealand lying 465 km south of the South Island.
Currently uninhabited, though archaeological finds on Enderby Island mark the most southerly known Polynesian outpost.
Designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1998 along with other New Zealand Subantarctic Islands.
e1159105983: The highest point in San Marino, part of the Apennines, with the capital city straddling its ridge.
Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2008 together with San Marino's historic centre.
Legend holds a small monastery stood on the mountain as early as the 8th century.
vQ65383: A tributary of the Northern Dvina flowing west through Russia's Komi Republic and Arkhangelsk Oblast.
Syktyvkar, the capital of the Komi Republic, is the largest city on its banks.
Briefly linked to the Kama/Volga system by the Northern Catherine Canal from 1822 until it fell out of use in 1838.
r1159102835: An island in the Arctic Sea between the Pechora Sea and the Kara Sea, off northern Russia.
Separated from the Russian mainland by the Yugorsky Strait and from Novaya Zemlya by the Kara Strait.
r1159104271: A vast geologic shield of exposed Precambrian igneous and metamorphic rock forming the ancient core of the North American continent.
Glaciation has left it with only a thin soil layer, exposing bedrock shaped by its long volcanic history.
Extends across central and eastern Canada and into the northern contiguous United States.
p1159104733: An island state within the Federated States of Micronesia, part of the Caroline Islands archipelago.
The smallest state of the FSM by both area and population.
Its capital is Tofol, and Mount Finkol is its highest point.
p1159105153: An island off Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula in the Caribbean Sea, near Playa del Carmen.
Designated a Pueblo Mágico by the Mexican government in 2023 for its cultural and historical importance.
e1159105919: The highest mountain on the Iberian Peninsula, part of the Sierra Nevada range in Spain's Penibaetic System.
Named after Abu'l-Hasan Ali, the penultimate Muslim ruler of Granada, said to be buried at its summit.
The highest peak in Southern Europe outside the Alps, climbable in a single day without major technical difficulty.
l1159123281: A large lake in Russia's Novgorod Oblast that formed part of the medieval trade route from the Varangians to the Greeks.
Veliky Novgorod lies just below its sole outflow, the Volkhov River.
Fed by 52 rivers, with the Volkhov draining it onward into Lake Ladoga and eventually the Gulf of Finland.
r1159102403: An Arctic Archipelago island in Nunavut, Canada's 15th-largest island, with its sole community at Gjoa Haven.
Visited and wintered over by several polar explorers searching for the Northwest Passage.
r1159104325: The region of South America drained by the Amazon River and its tributaries, spanning eight countries.
Covers the Amazon rainforest, the largest rainforest on Earth at about 6 million km2 and the most biodiverse region in the world.
Sparsely populated overall, aside from cities like Manaus and Belém, with many indigenous communities relying on fishing and agriculture.
l1159114279: A large, shallow lake in Uganda through which the Victoria Nile flows between Lake Victoria and Lake Albert.
Part of the African Great Lakes system, though not itself classed as one of the great lakes.
Much of its shallow water is covered by water lilies, papyrus and invasive water hyacinth, forming floating islands.
r1159103287: A large desert in the middle of the Iranian Plateau, the world's 24th-largest desert.
Stretches from the Alborz mountains to the Lut Desert, forming a natural barrier to east-west migration.
Spread across the Iranian provinces of Khorasan, Semnan, Tehran, Isfahan and Yazd.
p1159105151: A tiny, uninhabitable granite islet in the North Atlantic, far from any coast, west of Scotland's Outer Hebrides.
Formed during the Paleogene as part of the North Atlantic Igneous Province.
Nearby waters recorded a 29-metre wave in 2006, among the largest ever measured in the open ocean.
e1159108575: An extinct volcano in Bolivia's Oruro Department, the country's highest peak.
A composite volcano built from a stratovolcano atop several lava domes, within Sajama National Park.
Covered by an ice cap, with Polylepis tarapacana trees growing on its slopes up to 5,000 m.
m1159118475: A bight within the Gulf of Guinea on West Africa's coast, bordering Nigeria, Benin and Ghana.
Its shores were historically a major embarkation point in the Atlantic slave trade, giving the nearby coast its old name, the Slave Coast.
r1159102681: The westernmost of Hawaii's main islands, southwest of Kauai across the Kaulakahi Channel.
Privately purchased from the Kingdom of Hawaii in 1864 by Scottish plantation owner Elizabeth Sinclair.
The only place where Hawaiian remains the primary spoken language, undisplaced by English.
r1159103675: The northernmost point of the Eurasian continent and of mainland Russia, at the tip of the Taymyr Peninsula.
Lies just over 1,370 km from the North Pole.
r1159102913: The largest of the Kuril Islands, separating the Sea of Okhotsk from the North Pacific, claimed by both Russia and Japan.
Formally claimed as Japanese territory in 1855 before the Soviet Union occupied it in 1945 and expelled its Japanese residents.
Inhabited since at least the 14th century by the Indigenous Ainu people.
e1159108665: A mountain in Peru's Cordillera Blanca, whose southern summit is the highest point in Peru and in the entire tropics.
The fourth-highest peak in South America, after Aconcagua, Ojos del Salado and Monte Pissis.
vQ752674: A major tributary of the Amazon flowing through the Amazon rainforest in Brazil.
Once one of the largest clearwater rivers, now running as a sediment-laden whitewater river due to illegal gold mining and erosion.
Accounts for about 6% of the water in the Amazon basin.
m1159117135: A large, shallow bay of the Laccadive Sea between southeastern India and western Sri Lanka.
Separated from Palk Bay to the north by the chain of islets known as Adam's Bridge.
Home to the dugong, or sea cow.
r1159102687: The largest and most populous island of American Samoa, part of the Samoan Islands chain.
Home to Pago Pago, the territory's capital, situated on a large natural harbour.
Popular with tourists for its beaches, coral reefs and World War II relics.
r1159103885: A mountain range in the central Sahara, mostly in northern Chad, home to Emi Koussi, the highest point in both Chad and the Sahara.
Its central third is volcanic, with five peaks topped by large depressions formed by a continental hotspot active since the Oligocene.
Known as the domain of the Toubou people; its name means 'place where the mountain people live'.
r1159103811: The largest island in Vanuatu, usually called Santo, though less populous than Efate, home to the capital Port Vila.
Its only true town is Luganville.
xQ214924: The most powerful waterfall in Europe, on the High Rhine between the Swiss cantons of Schaffhausen and Zurich.
150 m wide and 23 m high, with summer water flow more than double the winter average.
A popular tourist attraction close to the border with Germany.
vQ651195: The largest and most water-abundant river in Kyrgyzstan, rising in the Tian Shan mountains.
Flows west through the Fergana Valley and merges with the Kara Darya in Uzbekistan to form the Syr Darya.
Dammed by several reservoirs for hydroelectricity, the largest being Kyrgyzstan's Toktogul Reservoir.
r1159102769: An island off Sumatra's east coast in the Java Sea, known historically for pepper and tin mining.
Controlled by Britain from 1812 until ceded to the Netherlands under the 1824 Anglo-Dutch Treaty.
Home to the UNESCO-recognised Belitung Geopark, with 17 designated tourist attractions.
r1159103377: An island in Russia's Severnaya Zemlya archipelago in the Arctic, named after the Soviet Bolshevik political faction.
Part of the Severnaya Zemlya archipelago, first mapped by Soviet expeditions in the 1930s.
r1159104201: A narrow mountain range in southcentral Alaska, home to Denali, the highest peak in North America.
One of the highest mountain ranges in the world, after the Himalayas and the Andes.
Stretches from Lake Clark to the White River in Canada's Yukon Territory.
p1159104837: The largest island of the US Virgin Islands, nicknamed 'Twin City' for its towns of Frederiksted and Christiansted.
Its highest point is Mount Eagle.
e1159105957: The highest point in the European part of the Netherlands, in the province of Limburg near the town of Vaals.
Lost its status as the Netherlands' overall highest point in 2010, when the volcanic Caribbean island of Saba was incorporated as a special municipality.
l1159114189: A lake on Russia's Taymyr Peninsula, lying south of the Byrranga Mountains.
One of the largest lakes north of the Arctic Circle, frozen for most of the year and drained by the Taymyra River.
xQ210280: Reputed to be the second most powerful waterfall in Europe after the Rhine Falls, in Iceland's Vatnajökull National Park.
Fed by the Jökulsá á Fjöllum river flowing from the Vatnajökull glacier, giving its water a greyish-white colour from sediment.
100 m wide with a 44 m drop into the Jökulsárgljúfur canyon.
r1159103265: The part of the Sahara lying east of the Nile River, bordered by the Gulf of Suez and the Red Sea.
Contains the Red Sea Hills mountain range running parallel to the coast.
Historically mined for building materials and precious metals, and crossed by trade routes to the Red Sea.
r1159104171: A volcanic mountain range about 1,200 km long in Inner Mongolia, China, and easternmost Mongolia.
Originally called the Xianbei Mountains, after the Xianbei people, a branch of the ancient Donghu.
e1159105847: A shield volcano that makes up much of South Korea's Jeju Island, the country's highest point.
Protected within Hallasan National Park and considered one of South Korea's three main mountains, along with Jirisan and Seoraksan.
m1159119119: A bay of the Arctic Ocean at the mouth of Russia's Ob River, considered the world's longest estuary.
Separates the Yamal Peninsula from the Gydan Peninsula in Russia's far north.
r1159102743: A leaf-shaped island separated from New Guinea by the narrow Muli Strait, part of Indonesia's South Papua province.
Known as Frederik Hendrik Island until 1963; Indonesia's 11th-largest island.
Home to about 11,000 people speaking Kolopom languages, with very low population density.
r1159104017: A peninsula in eastern China's Shandong province, between the Bohai Sea and the Yellow Sea.
Also known as the Jiaodong Peninsula.
e1159106011: A fell straddling the Norway-Finland border, whose Finnish side is the highest point in Finland.
The actual summit lies in Norway, just north of the border, due to a 1734 Swedish-Danish border treaty defined by natural features.
Ridnitšohkka, nearby, is the highest peak located entirely within Finland.
e1159106633: A stratovolcano on Norway's remote island of Jan Mayen, the world's northernmost active subaerial volcano.
The only active volcano in Norway, topped by a largely ice-filled crater about 1 km wide.
xQ38417: A series of seven cataracts along the Lualaba River in the DR Congo, formerly known as Stanley Falls.
The largest waterfall in the world by volume of annual flow, exceeding both Niagara and Iguazu Falls.
Below the falls the river becomes known as the Congo River; the last cataract is also called Wagenia Falls, after local fishermen.
r1159103251: A semidesert region of South Africa known for arid air, cloudless skies and extreme heat and cold.
Exposes fossil-rich rocks of the Karoo Supergroup, recording ecological change from the Middle Permian to Early Jurassic.
Historically formed a forbidding barrier between Cape Town and the interior Highveld.
r1159103623: A vast sandy desert in the south-central Sahara, spanning northeastern Niger to western Chad.
Bounded by the Aïr, Hoggar and Tibesti mountains and the basin of Lake Chad.
Was the centre of the Neolithic Tenerian culture and contains the dune field known as the Erg of Bilma.
l1159113621: Argentina's largest freshwater lake, in Patagonia within Los Glaciares National Park.
Fed by meltwater from glaciers including the Upsala and Perito Moreno glaciers, which carve 'trenches' into the lakebed where they meet the water.
Drains to the Atlantic Ocean via the Santa Cruz River.
m1159115729: A strait in the western Pacific between Luzon in the Philippines and Taiwan, linking the Philippine Sea to the South China Sea.
An important migratory corridor for seabirds and marine mammals, including humpback whales, fed by nutrient-rich Kuroshio Current water.
Distinct from the shallower Taiwan Strait between Taiwan and the Chinese mainland.
r1159103123: A physiographic province of the Appalachians running from Pennsylvania through Georgia.
Known for their blue haze, caused by isoprene released by the mountains' forests.
Home to Shenandoah and Great Smoky Mountains national parks, linked by the Blue Ridge Parkway.
r1159104083: The shortest overland route between the Gulf of Mexico and the Pacific Ocean, in southern Mexico.
Served as a major overland transport route between the two oceans before the Panama Canal opened.
Named for the town of Santo Domingo Tehuantepec, from a Nahuatl word meaning 'jaguar mountain'.
l1159126693: A brackish lagoon on the Baltic Sea, split between Poland and Russia's Kaliningrad exclave.
Separated from Gdańsk Bay by the narrow Vistula Spit.
r1159103037: A mountain range in northeastern Mongolia, within the Töv and Khentii provinces.
Considered part of the traditional Mongol homeland, in the region associated with the rise of Genghis Khan.
r1159104109: A low-lying flatland surrounding the northern Caspian Sea, part of the wider Aral-Caspian Depression.
Includes Karagiye near Aktau, at 132 m below sea level, the lowest point in the region.
xQ223649: A complex of seasonal waterfalls in South Africa's Drakensberg range, among the contenders for the world's tallest waterfall.
Its five free-leaping falls have a combined official drop of 948 m, though a 2016 survey measured it at 983 m.
Fed by the Tugela River, which rises on the Mont-Aux-Sources plateau.
r1159103713: A transboundary clay desert plateau shared by Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
Home to a semi-nomadic population herding camels, goats and sheep.
l1159113323: A deep glacial lake in Patagonia shared by Chile and Argentina, known as Lake Buenos Aires on the Argentine side.
Drains west to the Pacific via the Baker River, though it drained to the Atlantic during the last glaciation.
Enjoys an unusually sunny microclimate compared to the generally cold, humid surrounding region.
r1159103521: A mountain range in Morocco, part of the wider Atlas Mountains, running from the Atlantic coast to near Tafilalt.
Borders the Sahara to its south.
r1730073981: A vast steppe stretching from the northern Black Sea coast to the Caspian Sea, part of the larger Eurasian Steppe.
Corresponds to the lands of ancient Cimmeria, Scythia and Sarmatia.
Served for millennia as a corridor for nomadic horsemen, many of whom went on to conquer settled regions of Europe and Asia.
l1159123579: A reservoir forming a major part of the Panama Canal, carrying ships 33 km across the Isthmus of Panama.
Created in 1913 when the Gatun Dam's spillway gates were closed.
m1159119293: A tidal estuary of the Atlantic lying between Connecticut and Long Island, New York.
Forms part of the Intracoastal Waterway, stretching from the East River to Block Island Sound.
r1159103927: A mountain range in northwestern China separating the Tarim Basin from the Tibetan Plateau.
Its eastern section forms the border between Qinghai and the Xinjiang/Gansu region.
r1159104111: A vast swamp in South Sudan formed by the White Nile, one of the largest wetlands in the world.
Its dense vegetation historically blocked river navigation, stopping both ancient Egyptian and Roman expeditions from penetrating further south.
Its thick floating vegetation mats gave the swamp its name, from the Arabic word for 'barrier'.
r1159103059: A north-south mountain range extending the Hindu Kush system through western Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan.
Forms the eastern edge of the Iranian Plateau, bordering the Indus River Valley plains.
Its highest subrange peak, Koh-i-Zarghun, lies near Quetta in the Central Brahui Range.
l1159123301: Finland's fifth-largest lake, in the Kainuu region, nicknamed the 'Kainuu Sea'.
Drained by the Oulu River, which flows northwest into the Gulf of Bothnia.
r1159103263: A small desert in northern Kenya near the Ethiopian border, east of Lake Turkana.
Marsabit is its closest major urban centre.
p1159105003: A headland on Alaska's Arctic coast, northeast of Utqiagvik, the northernmost point of all US territory.
The northernmost point on the North American mainland, Murchison Promontory in Canada, lies 64 km farther north.
xQ639731: Austria's highest waterfall, on the Krimmler Ache river in the High Tauern National Park, Salzburg.
Has a total height of 380 m.
r1159103567: A mountain range in southern Siberia's Tuva Republic, curving along the Mongolian border.
Mentioned in 13th-century sources such as The Secret History of the Mongols under an earlier name.
l1159114537: A saltwater lake in Tibet, lying just west of Lake Manasarovar and south of Mount Kailash.
Sits at a lower elevation than nearby Lake Manasarovar, with the Sutlej River's source nearby.
xQ691557: A major source of the Ganges, in Uttarakhand, India, near the Tibetan border.
Its terminus, Gomukh, resembles a cow's mouth and is the precise source of the Bhagirathi river, a key Ganges tributary.
A traditional Hindu pilgrimage site, with devotees trekking to bathe in its icy waters.
r1159103231: A plateau in eastern India covering much of Jharkhand and parts of neighbouring states.
Bounded by the Indo-Gangetic Plain to the north and the Mahanadi River basin to the south.
l1159106925: A cold freshwater lake toward the south of Baffin Island, Nunavut, the world's largest lake situated on an island.
The largest lake in Nunavut, fed by Amadjuak Lake and draining west into Foxe Basin via the shallow Koukdjuak River.
Home to ringed seals and three recorded fish species, with surrounding tundra important for caribou calving.
l1159125013: A reservoir on the middle Volga and lower Kama rivers in Russia, the largest reservoir in Europe and third-largest in the world by area.
Created by the Zhiguli Hydroelectric Station dam, filled between 1955 and 1957.
Its filling submerged several towns, including the old fortress town of Stavropol-on-Volga, replaced by the city of Tolyatti.
vQ386331: A river in south-central Brazil, rising in the Mantiqueira Mountains and joining the Paranaíba River to form the Upper Paraná.
Its basin generates about 67% of the energy produced in Minas Gerais state.
Interrupted by several dams and reservoirs, including the Furnas and Peixotos dams.
r1159103107: A series of mountain ranges in Wales, named from the country's Latin name Cambria.
Now usually refers to the Elenydd uplands of Mid Wales, a sparsely populated area sometimes called the 'Desert of Wales'.
Includes the sources of the River Severn and River Wye; Plynlimon is its highest point at 752 m.
m1159118537: A sound off the Gulf of Alaska on the Kenai Peninsula, home to the port of Valdez, terminus of the Trans-Alaska Pipeline.
Contains numerous small islands and settlements including Cordova and Whittier.
r1730072879: A peninsula in Quebec, Canada, on the south side of the St. Lawrence River, separated from New Brunswick by Chaleur Bay.
Its name comes from the Mi'kmaq word gespe'g, meaning 'end of the land'.
Slightly larger in area than Belgium.
xQ38432: The largest waterfall in China, on the Liuzhi River in Guizhou province.
Its main drop is the biggest waterfall in Asia by height.
m1159119471: An estuary in southeastern Louisiana, despite its name, connecting to the Gulf of Mexico through the Rigolets strait.
Named in 1699 by French explorer Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville after a minister of Louis XIV.
Forms the core of the Pontchartrain Basin, one of the largest wetland systems on the Gulf Coast.
r1159103649: A desert and steppe region in Inner Mongolia, China, comprising the Kubuqi Desert in the north and Mu Us Desert in the south.
Wedged between the arable Hetao region and the Loess Plateau, with soil poorly suited to farming.
xQ1266055: A waterfall on the Blue Nile in Ethiopia's Amhara Region, known locally as Tis Abay, meaning 'great smoke'.
Its flow has been greatly reduced since 2003, when a hydroelectric station diverted much of the river except in the rainy season.
Isolates Lake Tana's ecology from the rest of the Nile, contributing to the evolution of endemic species in the lake.
r1159102625: A vast salt pan in Botswana's savanna, one of the largest salt flats in the world, remnant of the long-vanished Lake Makgadikgadi.
Human mitochondrial DNA studies suggest modern Homo sapiens may have begun evolving in this region around 200,000 years ago, when it was a fertile lake-studded landscape.
r1159103631: A large field of sand dunes in the Sahara, mostly in northeastern Algeria, the second-largest erg in the country.
Borders the Atlas and Aurès Mountains to the north and spills over into Tunisia.
r1159104315: A vast grassland region of Central Asia spanning northern Kazakhstan and parts of Russia, also called the Great Steppe.
Forms the central and western part of the wider Eurasian Steppe, between the Pontic-Caspian steppe and the Emin Valley steppe.
Known as the Kirghiz Steppe before the mid-19th century.
r1159102981: A mountain range in Belize and eastern Guatemala, in Central America.
Largely covered by tropical rainforest and home to protected wildlife areas including the Cockscomb Basin.
r1159103533: A major mountain range crossing Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador and Honduras, known in Mexico as the Sierra Madre de Chiapas.
Part of the American Cordillera, the chain forming the western backbone of the Americas.
r1159103283: An extremely arid desert plateau in southeastern Afghanistan, also known as the Sistan Desert.
Sparsely inhabited by Baluch and Pashtun nomads; a 1998 drought displaced around 100,000 of them.
Gradually encroaching westward onto surrounding agricultural land.
vQ968640: Flows from Oregon's high desert through the Cascade Range and Klamath Mountains to California's Pacific coast.
The third-largest salmon and steelhead producing river on the US West Coast.
Holds deep cultural significance for Native American tribes, whose lands along the river saw violent displacement during the California Gold Rush.
xQ673150: A temperate maritime glacier on New Zealand's South Island, descending from the Southern Alps within Te Wāhipounamu World Heritage Site.
Lies alongside the Fox Glacier about 20 km to the south; its terminal feeds the Waiho River.
r1159103981: The largest river delta in Europe, where the Volga River drains into the Caspian Sea in Russia's Astrakhan Oblast.
Has grown dramatically over the 20th century, from about 3,222 km2 in 1880 to over 27,000 km2 today, due to changes in Caspian Sea level.
Lies in an arid climate zone with strong winds that form linear dunes across the delta.
xQ583591: A valley glacier on the northern slopes of the Mont Blanc massif in the French Alps.
The longest and largest glacier in France when its tributary glaciers are included, second only to the Aletsch Glacier in the Alps overall.
xQ3361971: One of the tallest waterfalls in Europe and the eighth-tallest in the world, in Norway's Møre og Romsdal county.
A tiered horsetail waterfall fed by the Vinnufonna glacier, flowing into the Driva river.
r1159103633: A field of sand dunes in the northern-central Algerian Sahara, also called the Western Sand Sea.
The third-largest erg in Algeria, after Erg Chech and the Grand Erg Oriental.
xQ37319: The tallest waterfall in Oregon, dropping in two tiers over basalt cliffs in the Columbia River Gorge.
Attracts over two million visitors a year, making it the most-visited natural recreation site in the US Pacific Northwest.
Its 1914 footbridge and 1925 lodge are both listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
xQ855226: A glacier in the Karakoram range in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan, one of the largest in the entire range.
Flows southeast from the central Karakoram crest; its accumulation zone of permanent snow and ice makes up 68% of its total basin area.
xQ391165: One of six glaciers flowing from the Columbia Icefield in the Canadian Rockies, the most visited glacier in North America.
Has receded over 1.5 km and lost more than half its volume in the past 125 years.
Hidden crevasses on its surface have caused tourist deaths, despite its easy accessibility.
xQ1632936: A glacier spanning Wrangell-St. Elias National Park in Alaska and Kluane National Park in Yukon, Canada.
xQ1920336: A glacier near Juneau, Alaska, within the federally protected Mendenhall Glacier Recreation Area in the Tongass National Forest.
Has retreated 1.75 miles since Mendenhall Lake formed in 1929, and continues to lose mass as temperatures rise.
